div.div:
Consumer crashed before the DB write
• Auto-ack — the message is lost
• Manual ack after commit — it goes back to the queue (redelivered), nothing is lost
• Crashed after commit, before ack — a duplicate. Hence idempotency: message_id in processed_messages in the same transaction
Exception without ack/nack
The message stays unacked while the channel lives. 10 of them (prefetch) — the consumer stalls. consumer_timeout is 30 min. So always nack explicitly in catch.
Poison message
Transient error — retry queue with TTL. Permanent error or x-delivery-limit (20 in 4.x) — DLX → DLQ, alert.
Options and their cost
• Ack before processing: simple, fast. Cost — loss on crash
• Ack after commit + idempotency: no loss. Cost — inbox table, dedup
• Quorum instead of classic: survives a node failure. Cost — disk, network, lower throughput
• Outbox on the producer: no loss between DB and publish. Cost — a table, a relay, latency
What breaks first at ×10
1. processed_messages grows — TTL cleanup, partition by date
2. Prefetch: large — a burst of redeliveries on crash, small — lower throughput
3. Consumer DB down — messages burn through the limit and land in the DLQ: add backoff or a circuit breaker
